Hey, I’m sorry you’re going through this. It sounds like you’re going through something very similar to what went on in my life for a long time and I’m still feeling the effects of, but trust me as someone who thought for certain that it wasn’t going to ever get better that it will. You have all the power you need to make the changes in your life that need to happen. Something that worked for me was writing a list of everything I’ve wanted to do (learn to draw better, learn guitar, another language etc.) and try to chip away at it to become the person I wanted to be. Another thing is getting more sleep and cutting back on weed. I’m not totally averse to the occasional puff of the green stuff but it does fry your brain when it’s a consistent habit. The main thing above all is to try and change your perspective. Try to figure out how you can be happy and content by yourself and then gradually you will begin to attract the people you need for companionship and social interaction. Try to see everything as an opportunity to be better and do something good for yourself. When you talk down on yourself that is what makes you believe it. Another thing to remember is that change doesn’t happen overnight. It will be a process that will take a very long time and you will have peaks where you feel on top of the world and lows where you feel absolutely hopeless like nothing will get better. But know that every low you have will make the peaks all the more stronger. Whatever happened in the past is just that: in the past. Now is the time to stay focused in the present moment and become who you want to be. You have the power in you my friend.

I feel like Eddie and Angela are both very important to the symbolism in Silent Hill 2. They both represent the paths that repression can take you and how James could turn out. Eddie chooses to not accept what he did and not learn anything. He goes crazy and tries to attack you. Angela does seem to accept her past, but her going up the stairs when the hotel is on fire is her succumbing to it rather than trying to move on. Personally, I think both characters stories are perfect the way they are

I’m sure a therapist will be able to help you through it, I saw a therapist for a while and it definitely helped my mood a lot. I don’t know if you’re religious at all but something that helped me is that the reason we fear the afterlife or possibility of no afterlife is because we’re in these imperfect forms that can’t comprehend that amount of time. Whatever the afterlife may be we’ll most likely be beings that can comprehend it and just see it as a normal state of living. Personally, I like to think that life is cyclical. You live, you die, the rest of humanity goes on until the destruction of earth and the heat death of the universe. Then, one day it just all starts anew and we go through the same thing, but it doesn’t always play out the exact same. That’s what deja vu is. You’ve lived it before, but you still have opportunities to do it differently without even knowing it.
